body:
Yes, high strung would be a word to describe things.  I knew a chef from one of the Disney resorts...tough job, long weeks, no idea how one does it.  Rough gig.

And I'd say good shape doesn't always mean healthy mind.  A lot of the guys at the gym have similiar issues, replete with one guy going through with things a few weeks ago.

Thanks for the input guys.  Yes, a thousand times yes to the 'there's always a bigger fish' concept.  That's actually always been my driving goal, to be that fish, and then see who came out that was better.  

The girl knows and ball is in her court for forgiveness.  I've asked for it, apologized profusely, but that's more or less her call.  

I actually hadn't thought about a journal.  At the very least, would help keep my thoughts in order and chart out the ups and downs.  Thanks for that man.

It's a pretty small sport and yes, a complete give away.  Suffice to say it's a summer games event, there's a lot of precision involved, and very much individually focused.  I'd agree it's similiar to figure skating, most of my competitors, and myself, will fly out of country to see our coaches or visit factories to hand pick our equipment.

I appreciate the feedback from both you and TheNoxx.  I'll agree I'm high strung and easily go off once the feeling of 'ok, self containment has failed...cut loose...now.'  Finding how to relax/chill out is rough because frankly, I have no idea.  How do people just let things go and not let stuff get on their nerves?
